title: The Practice of Art and AI
editor: Andreas J. Hirsch, Markus Jandl, Gerfried Stocker

description.main: A Hatje Cantz volume published with the 42nd Ars Electronica Festival that documents work from the European ARTificial Intelligence Lab. It looks at how artistic practice engages artificial intelligence, with around 500 photographs.
description.extended:
A record of the European ARTificial Intelligence Lab, the Ars Electronica programme that places artists and AI research side by side, published for the 42nd Ars Electronica Festival in Linz.

The book documents projects that examine art, technology and society through the advance of artificial intelligence. It is edited by Andreas J. Hirsch, Markus Jandl and Gerfried Stocker, with texts by Hirsch, and carries some 500 photographs across 307 pages in English. Gerhard Kirchschläger designed it. Hatje Cantz lists it as a paperback, 168 by 238 mm, issued in autumn 2021.

The book covers the work of 13 cultural and six scientific institutions that took part in the lab.

notes: Hatje Cantz lists 307 pages; Google Books lists 301, and some retailers date it February 2022 against the publisher's autumn 2021. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
